walkthroughs.body_html: AU for Solar System distances. Light-year for stars and nearby galaxies. Parsec (3.26 ly) for stellar/galactic distances. 1 megaparsec (Mpc) ~3.26 million ly is used for galaxies.
Measure a nearby star's shift against distant background as Earth orbits. Bigger shift means closer star. Works out to a few thousand light-years with modern data (Gaia mission).
Cepheid variables and Type Ia supernovae have known luminosities. Comparing actual brightness to apparent brightness gives distance — works across galaxies and the universe.
